I totally relate - comparing everyday buys really is an ongoing battle of cost-effectivens and quality!

When weighing those two factors - cost & longevity - the cheaper item is often tempting. For a one-time expense on say a new toaster, I'd usually choose a more durable brand even for $x-$2 higher up-front since it should save me the headache (and extra $x-4 in the short-run if/ when that toaster needs to replaced) in about y years' worth of repairs and new replacements over its less expensive counterparts in the store (which often don" last 9 or more moths in heavy home kitchen wear & use, vs. brand names holding out over many more years.)

The one time I actually bought that cheaper thing and regreted it most recently was for new winter gloves for cold outdoor work & chores in my yard
